title: Finite scalar-perfect generation after the finite discrete comparison
statement: Let A be a finite discrete commutative ring and Λ a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with a ring-object isomorphism Λ ≅ Cont(-,A). Let X be a separated finite-type scheme over any field k [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Every K in Dctf(X,Λ) [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] belongs, for some n, to the retract closure of the n-fold extension product of the integer-shift closure of the objects i_!P, where i:S→X is a locally closed immersion and P is pro-etale locally the constant scalar realization of a bounded finite-projective Λ(*)-complex [def-sfb-locally-perfect-scalar-model, def-sfb-scalar-perfect-generators]. Here i_! is exactly the open-image-extension followed by the right-derived closed module pushforward of [def-sfb-scalar-perfect-generators]. The finite shift/extension/retract closure is the finitary closure of [sk-def-localizing-closure], without coproduct closure. The coefficient rings and the scalar change functor are those of [def-sfb-scalar-six-coefficient-interfaces].

proof.text:
finite discrete condensed and scheme ring comparisons identify the
coefficient sheaf with the constant ring sheaf. Apply the normalized exact equivalence
of module categories and its derived equivalence to K. Finite constant models become
finite locally constant ordinary modules on the same strata, and Tor amplitude is
unchanged because the equivalence is monoidal. Apply proEtale_flatConstructible_thickGeneration.
Its generators are locally constant finite-projective modules in degree zero. On a
trivializing cover the corresponding scalar module is a retract of a finite free
module, so its single complex is a locally perfect scalar model. The comparison of
ordinary and internal open extension and closed direct image identifies their locally
closed extensions with sfbLocallyClosedDerivedExtension. Rotate each cone to an
extension and use the finite extension-product identities to collect summands at the
end. Finite sums are split extensions, so no infinite closure is introduced. Finally
transport along e; coefficient isomorphisms preserve the splittings, local scalar
models, and the normalized extension functors. The zero ring, empty stratum and rank
zero use the same splittings. The nodes used by this native-presentation argument are [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant], [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant], [det-sf-flat-model-generation].
